issues.description: The problem UML and description expect Stock to provide a method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). However, the template Stock class defines a method addItem(StockIngredient) instead, while the reference solution implements addToStockIngredients. This name/signature mismatch can confuse students about which method to call/implement and may cause compilation errors if tests or the expected design use addToStockIngredients.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template's addItem(StockIngredient) method to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or add an addToStockIngredients wrapper that delegates to addItem) so the template matches the UML/specification and the reference solution. Update any references in the template to use the standardized method name.

issues.description: The problem statement's class diagram and the solution expect a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient). This is a naming mismatch for the same concept (adding a StockIngredient to the stock) and can confuse students when mapping the UML/problem requirements to the provided template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or provide a wrapper addToStockIngredients that delegates to addItem) so the template, problem diagram, and solution use the same identifier for adding a StockIngredient.
